source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Respect the capable client’s refusal, document the relevant information and decision according to policy, and communicate the refusal to the responsible clinician or team.","B":"Proceed with the treatment because a capable client’s refusal becomes invalid whenever the clinical team believes the expected benefit is substantial.","C":"Ask a family member to override the refusal because informed refusal applies only when the healthcare team agrees with the client’s choice.","D":"Document only the words “client refused” and omit the information provided before the decision because that discussion has no relevance to the record."}}
source_row.rationale: Patient-rights and informed-consent standards recognize the patient’s right to participate in decisions and to give or withhold informed consent. Nursing actions should respect the decision and follow organizational/legal documentation and communication processes.
source_row.source_detail: Hospital Patient Rights CoP — 42 CFR 482.13(b)(2); informed consent policy/process and patient participation in care decisions. CMS QSO-24-10-Hospitals posted 2024-04-01; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. source_row.source_name: CMS — Hospital Interpretive Guidelines for Informed Consent
source_row.stem: A client with decision-making capacity refuses a recommended treatment after receiving information about the treatment, expected benefits, material risks, and alternatives. What should the nurse do?
